sn46.6:1.1: See note on [sn2.18:1.2]() for this location.
sn46.6:1.2: Kuṇḍaliya (“the ear-ringed”) is not known elsewhere.
sn46.6:3.4: The text uses three synonyms: _citta_ (“mind”), _mānasa_ (“spirit”), and _cetasa_ (“heart”). | Read _apatitthīnacitto_ (“mind unirritated”) per BJT, and the Thai and PTS variants for the parallel passage at [mnd10:92.7](). The verb form _patiṭṭhiyati_ appears in [pli-tv-pvr17:172.3]() with a list of terms for anger. | “Undaunted spirit” (_adīnamanasa_) is also at [thag3.9:1.4]() and [thag15.1:11.4](). However, the texts waver between reading _adīna_ (“undaunted”) and _alīna_ (“not sluggish”, for which the meaning is established at [snp1.3:34.2]()). The parallel to this passage at [mnd10:92.7]() reads _alīna_ in MS, but _adīna_ in Thai and PTS editions. The confusion extends to the commentaries, which for the present passage glosses, “mind not daunted (_adīnacitta_) by the power of displeasure”, while at [thag3.9:1.4]() they have, “non-overthrown by laziness, etc., not sluggish mind (_alīnacitta_), not living lazily”. See too _dīnamana_ (“disheartened”) at [dn18:4.17]().
